agent.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answer "To a quiet house in Babylon" is invented rather than being a real detail from somewhere in the Bible. Babylon is biblical, but a quiet house there is not.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

agent.problem: The question uses verse 22 when it tells that Amon did evil and served and sacrificed to Manasseh's idols, but the card cites only verse 23. Verse 22 is not told or cited on any other card, so the citation does not cover all the material this card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

agent.problem: Marking the statement False establishes only that the people did not release the conspirators. No card tells what verse 25 actually says happened: the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against Amon. The walkthrough then moves directly to Josiah, leaving out that event.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: Too many of this stop's choices depend on luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 3, 10, 13, 15, 16, 19 and 20 give no earlier-card basis for knowing God's response, whether the people stop using the high places, Manasseh's burial place, Amon's reign length, whether Amon humbles himself, how the people treat the conspirators, or Josiah's name. These seven discovery questions make up most of the stop's thirteen choice cards, and card 18's exact outcome of the conspiracy is also unsupported.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
